question: *Mycobacterium leprae* can be cultured on Löwenstein-Jensen medium if incubated at 33°C for an extended period of 12 weeks.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. *M. leprae* is the only significant human mycobacterial pathogen that cannot be grown on ANY artificial medium. Unlike *M. tuberculosis* (which grows on LJ medium in 4–8 weeks), no modification of temperature, medium, or duration enables in vitro culture of *M. leprae*. It is an obligate intracellular organism — diagnosis relies on slit-skin smear and histopathology, not culture.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! *M. leprae* CANNOT be cultured on any artificial medium — not LJ, not Middlebrook 7H10/7H11, not any synthetic medium regardless of temperature or incubation time. This is unique among human mycobacterial pathogens. It can only be propagated in mouse foot-pads (Shepard's method) and nine-banded armadillos.
